title: Cyrus and the Landfall
premise: Salvage diver Cyrus Eriksen is quietly working a forbidden wreck off the coast of Vessany when the tide drains away to reveal a sea cave holding the wreck's true cargo—and proof that the navy scuttled the ship deliberately, drowning its own crew to bury a smuggling scandal. Hunted by both the navy and a ruthless salvage fleet captain who wants the cargo silenced, Cyrus must choose between selling out and vanishing, or surfacing the truth for the drowned crew's forgotten families. Racing six tides before the dry season closes the reef, Cyrus allies with a disgraced naval archivist and the wreck's last living survivor's granddaughter, and in the final confrontation at the cave mouth, chooses justice over survival—exposing the scandal at the cost of the salvage that was supposed to clear their debt. The book ends with Cyrus penniless but no longer invisible, claimed at last by a community that knows their name.
about_author: D. M. Reyes spent a decade as a marine surveyor in Southeast Asian ports before turning to fiction full-time. They write adventure stories about people who live on the water's edge of the law, drawing on real wrecks, real tides, and the quiet economies of coastal towns.

chapters.title: Six Fathoms Down
chapters.summary: Cyrus dives the navy-cordoned wreck alone at dawn, salvaging brass and a sealed strongbox while dodging patrol boats. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness—we see they work invisible by design, and like it that way.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector
chapters.summary: Back in port, harbor boss Ondine Marrec calls in Cyrus's debt: one more season or the boat goes. A navy officer named Lt. Halloway posts a reward for 'unauthorized salvage.' POV: Cyrus. Beat: pressure tightening; invisibility has a price tag.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gave Back
chapters.summary: An extreme low tide exposes a cave beneath the wreck. Inside: intact cargo hold, personal effects of the crew, and a captain's log proving the ship was scuttled with souls aboard. POV: Cyrus. Beat: awe curdling into dread—the find everyone would kill for.

chapters.title: The Log of the Meridian Star
chapters.summary: Cyrus reads the log by lamplight: orders from above, a deliberate flooding, survivors abandoned. The names of ninety-one dead stare back. POV: Cyrus. Beat: moral weight lands; this stopped being salvage.

chapters.title: A Woman Who Reads Wrecks
chapters.summary: Cyrus seeks out Sefa Ilori, granddaughter of the Meridian Star's surviving quartermaster, now a disgraced naval archivist who's spent years requesting files that keep coming back redacted. POV: Sefa. Beat: two lonely obsessives recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Ninety-One Names
chapters.summary: Sefa matches log entries to missing-persons records; families were paid hush money and scattered. One name belongs to her grandfather's brother. POV: Sefa. Beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: The Fleet Arrives
chapters.summary: Captain Renn Vosk's salvage fleet anchors in port, contracted by someone high up to 'clear' the site before dry season. Vosk buys drinks, asks questions, remembers faces. POV: Cyrus. Beat: the clock starts—six tides.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Sefa plan to copy the log and evidence out through the cave on the next big low tide. Halloway tails them; they barely lose him in the fish market. POV: alternating. Beat: conspiracy becomes partnership becomes trust.

chapters.title: Tide Two
chapters.summary: First dive into the cave with Sefa's grandson piloting. They recover the log and a ledger of payoffs—but Vosk's divers are already sweeping the outer wreck. POV: Cyrus. Beat: triumph undercut by the sense of being hunted.

chapters.title: Vosk Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Vosk corners Cyrus privately: hand over the documents, take a cut, disappear rich. He mentions Ondine's debt, making it clear he owns half the port already. POV: Cyrus. Beat: temptation with teeth—the easy way out.

chapters.title: What Ondine Knows
chapters.summary: Cyrus confronts Ondine, who admits she sold information about Cyrus's dives years ago to survive after her husband drowned on a navy contract. POV: Ondine. Beat: betrayal reframed as shared survival; the theme sharpens.

chapters.title: Tide Three
chapters.summary: Recovery dive goes wrong when a navy patrol floods the reef with sonar; Sefa's grandson takes a propeller wash hit getting them out. POV: Sefa. Beat: first blood—the cost of the cause becomes real.

chapters.title: Halloway's Doubt
chapters.summary: Lt. Halloway, ordered to bury the file he himself once flagged, quietly leaves an unredacted page where Sefa will find it. POV: Halloway. Beat: the system contains its own cracks; an enemy becomes ambiguous.

chapters.title: Tide Four
chapters.summary: They photograph everything and stash copies in three places. Vosk burns down Ondine's office as a message. POV: Cyrus. Beat: escalation; there's no longer a version of this where everyone walks away.

chapters.title: The Survivor's Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Sefa tells Cyrus her family story—her great-uncle's letters, the hush money her grandmother refused. She asks Cyrus why they're really doing this. POV: Sefa. Beat: Cyrus admits it's not about the debt anymore; it's about mattering.

chapters.title: Tide Five
chapters.summary: Penultimate dive: they go for the ship's bell and the admiral's signed order stenciled inside the strongbox. Vosk's divers ambush them in the cave; a fight in the dark, and Cyrus barely escapes with the order. POV: Cyrus. Beat: victory purchased with near-drowning and a broken dive mask.

chapters.title: No Way Out That Doesn't Cost
chapters.summary: Halloway warns them: tomorrow the navy seals the reef permanently, and Vosk sails at dawn. One tide left. Sefa proposes going public; Cyrus calculates they'll all hang for theft first. POV: alternating. Beat: despair, then resolve.

chapters.title: The Last Low Tide
chapters.summary: Final dive at slack water before dawn: Cyrus descends alone to place the evidence where the whole fleet can see it—lashed to the wreck's exposed superstructure, lit by strobes, under water too shallow to hide. POV: Cyrus. Beat: the climax begins; a choice made with the body before the mind consents.

chapters.title: Wreck of the Meridian Star
chapters.summary: Vosk tries to dynamite the evidence; Halloway, choosing his oath over his career, arrests him mid-act as Sefa broadcasts the ledger to every port radio in range. The families arrive by boat, dozens of them. POV: Sefa. Beat: chaos resolving into reckoning.

chapters.title: Ninety-One Bells
chapters.summary: A memorial dive: the recovered bell rung ninety-one times above the wreck as families watch from a hundred boats. The navy, cornered, opens an inquiry. POV: Cyrus. Beat: catharsis; the drowned get their names back.

chapters.title: Settled
chapters.summary: Ondine tears up the debt—not charity, she says, but payment for what Cyrus's silence cost her. Halloway resigns rather than sign the cover-up's final page. POV: Cyrus. Beat: accounts balanced, debts honored, the old life closed.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Dry season ends; the reef closes. Cyrus, boatless and broke, is offered a berth on Sefa's family boat and a place in a town that now knows their name. They sail out past the buoy one last time. POV: Cyrus. Beat: belonging earned, not found—invisibility traded for home.
